name: Theophylline
route_note: Modified-release oral tablets/capsules; IV as aminophylline for acute severe disease; dosing guided by serum levels
originator: Natural product (tea); first synthesised by Wilhelm Traube

discovery.note: Isolated from tea leaves; chemically synthesised by Traube in 1900; bronchodilator effect recognised in the 1920s.

tagline: Old methylxanthine bronchodilator with a narrow therapeutic window
summary: Theophylline is a methylxanthine related to caffeine that relaxes bronchial smooth muscle and has modest anti-inflammatory effects. Once a first-line asthma drug, it is now reserved as add-on therapy because of its narrow therapeutic range and many drug interactions.
mechanism: Theophylline non-selectively inhibits phosphodiesterases (notably PDE3 and PDE4), raising cAMP and cGMP in airway smooth muscle and inflammatory cells, which relaxes the bronchi.

It also antagonises adenosine A1 and A2 receptors, which underlies stimulant, diuretic and some toxic effects such as seizures and arrhythmias. At low concentrations it may activate histone deacetylase-2, restoring corticosteroid responsiveness.
uses: Acute severe asthma (IV aminophylline, limited role)
Apnoea of prematurity (largely replaced by caffeine)

history.title: Isolation
history.detail: Albrecht Kossel isolates theophylline from tea.

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Wilhelm Traube reports a chemical synthesis.

history.title: Bronchodilator
history.detail: Its effect in asthma is first reported.

history.title: IV aminophylline
history.detail: Intravenous aminophylline is shown to relieve acute asthma.

history.title: Therapeutic drug monitoring
history.detail: During the 1970s serum-level-guided dosing becomes standard, improving safety.

history.title: Declining role
history.detail: From the 1990s inhaled corticosteroids and beta2-agonists displace theophylline as first-line asthma therapy.

pk.half_life: ~8 h in non-smoking adults (highly variable; shorter in smokers, longer in neonates, liver disease, heart failure)

serious: Toxicity from interactions (e.g. ciprofloxacin, fluvoxamine, erythromycin, smoking cessation)

facts: Theophylline is one of the methylxanthines in tea, alongside caffeine and theobromine.
Smoking induces CYP1A2, so stopping smoking can raise theophylline levels into the toxic range.
